title: Private delta-sync & state-quiesce controller for staged upgrades and safe rollbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers require zero-downtime, auditable upgrades across heterogeneous clusters and air-gapped environments. Existing migration tooling relies on monolithic runbooks and manual quiesce operations that are error-prone for stateful components (database schema changes, KV backend sharding, and agent/sidecar restarts).

Goal: Build a delta-sync + state-quiesce controller that enables: (1) safe staged rollouts across LTS channels and ephemeral release tracks, (2) transactional data migrations with dry-run and checksum verification, (3) cohort-based canaries with automatic rollback on quality or SLO regressions, and (4) deterministic pause/resume with a repair/rehydration path for interrupted migrations.

Scope: This ticket covers design and initial implementation of the controller and supporting CLI/harness for private deployments (on-prem & VPC). It will integrate with release-channel metadata, rollout gates, and the upgrade policy engine in the control plane. The controller is intentionally decoupled from the lower-level helm/k8s operator tasks so it can run in air-gapped clusters as a lightweight daemonset (go binary).
progress_updates: 2025-01-14: Kickoff — worked session with Release Eng, Platform, and Security to outline constraints for air-gapped installs. Identified critical path: state quiesce primitives + delta-sync algorithm.

2025-01-21: Spike completed — prototype delta-sync that computes patch sets for agent configs and bin diffs. Verified checksums across a 3-node onprem lab cluster. Spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/spikes/delta-sync-spike (internal).

2025-01-28: Implemented controller scaffold and CRD (UpgradePlan). Implemented first two phases: PREPARE (quiesce), DELTA_APPLY. Unit tests added for idempotency. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/187
2025-02-03: Canary cohort logic wired to rollout engine. Added health probes and SLO watchdog integration. Began QA on cluster with mixed LTS channels (1.18-LTS and 1.19-stable).
decisions: Use a two-phase state quiesce model: QUIESCE → SNAPSHOT → DELTA_APPLY → VALIDATE → UNQUIESCE. Snapshots stored as compressed artifacts (sha256) to allow independent verification and rollback.

Delta-sync transport will use a content-addressed chunk store over HTTPS with optional airgap bundle export/import. In air-gapped installs, operators will supply the bundle via 'upgradectl import-bundle'.
Canary cohorts will be defined by 'cohort affinity' labels (node-pool, customer-shard, region). Default cohort sizes: 5% → 25% → 100% with configurable SLO thresholds per cohort.

Rollback strategy: automated rollback on failing pre-defined quality gates (regression in latency >10% or error rate increase >2x). For data migrations, rollback requires replayable compensating transactions — we will implement a repair-runner to rehydrate nodes that roll back mid-migration.
Compatibility shims for agent protocol will be included to allow mixed-version KV traffic for a bounded overlap window (90 days) to support staggered customer upgrades.
risks: Stateful migrations are inherently risky — if snapshot/restore fails during network partition we must ensure no partial writes leave the system inconsistent.
Air-gapped installs increase operational complexity; operators may misapply bundles. We'll add checksum verification and a gated 'apply' confirmation step.
Performance impact during quiesce window if snapshotting large KV stores — may require background incremental checkpoints and throttled IO.
technical_notes: UpgradePlan CRD fields: target_version, lts_channel, cohort_selector, preflight_checks (list), delta_strategy (chunked|rsync-like), dry_run boolean, rollback_policy.
StateQuiesce controller will expose a gRPC control plane for local agents to coordinate quiesce/unquiesce and to stream snapshot manifests. Agents must implement idempotent quiesce hooks.
Delta-sync algorithm: compute minimal byte-range diffs for model artifacts, use deduping via content-addressed chunks to minimize transfer for large model files.
SLO watchdog integration: push cohort telemetry to release console via the 'upgrade-metrics' event stream (metric names: upgrade.latency_p50, upgrade.errors, upgrade.applied_cohort).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end upgrade of a 3-node private cluster from 2024.12 → 2025.02 (different LTS channels) without manual intervention except operator 'approve' for production cohort.
Dry-run mode validates patch set and reports checksums for all changed artifacts.
Automated rollback triggers on simulated SLO regression in the canary cohort and produces a repair-runner job to reconcile state on rolled-back nodes.
Air-gap bundle import workflow documented and validated in test lab.
comments: Priya Nair (PM) — 2025-01-22: Love the cohort affinity idea. Please add a clear operator override so customers can abort a staged rollout before cohort 2 if they're running compliance windows.
Liam Chen (Security) — 2025-01-24: Ensure all snapshot artifacts are encrypted with KMS keys; air-gapped bundle manifest must include signed provenance metadata. Security review required before GA.
Morgan Blake (Platform) — 2025-01-30: Suggest adding a 'repair dry-run' that simulates rehydration to detect migration-order issues early.
